title: Air-fryer chicken Caesar wrap
subtitle: Seasoned air-fried chicken breast sliced and wrapped with Caesar-dressed leaves.
excerpt: Chicken breast air-fried until golden and juicy, sliced and wrapped in a tortilla with romaine, Caesar dressing, and parmesan. Serves two.
sourceNotes: The Caesar salad was created by Caesar Cardini in Tijuana, Mexico in 1924 and became the basis for numerous British lunch preparations including the Caesar wrap, which appeared widely in British supermarkets and high-street cafes from the early 2000s.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook the chicken ahead and refrigerate; assemble the wrap cold.

content.text: The chicken for a Caesar wrap needs to be juicy rather than crisp ,  cook at 200°C and rest for 3 minutes before slicing. Butterfly the breast (slice it horizontally most of the way through and open it flat) so both halves cook to the same thickness at the same time. A 200 g breast that isn't butterflied takes 18-20 minutes and the edges overcook before the centre is done.

Rub the {{chicken-breast}} butterflied breasts with {{olive-oil}} of olive oil, {{garlic-powder}} of garlic powder, {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt, and cracked black pepper. Preheat the air fryer to 200°C. Cook for 7 minutes, flip, and cook for a further 6-7 minutes until cooked through with no pink when cut at the thickest part. Rest for 3 minutes then slice across the grain.

Warm the {{tortilla-wrap}} tortillas in a dry frying pan or microwave. Lay out each tortilla and add a portion of {{cos-lettuce}} romaine, {{parmesan}} of grated parmesan, {{caesar-dressing}} of Caesar dressing, and the sliced chicken. Fold the sides in and roll into a tight wrap. Cut on the diagonal and serve.

items.fix: Butterfly the breast before cooking so it is the same thickness throughout. Check after 13 minutes and pull as soon as it is no longer pink at the thickest part.

items.cause: Filling too wet or not wrapped tightly.
items.fix: Drain any excess dressing from the leaves before filling. Roll firmly, tuck the ends in, and chill the assembled wrap for 10 minutes before cutting if it is to be served cold.
Warm the tortilla briefly before assembling ,  15 seconds in the microwave makes it pliable and less likely to split.

content.text: The chicken Caesar wrap is a reliable packed lunch or quick midweek meal. The air-fried chicken can be cooked the night before and refrigerated, making assembly the next day a 5-minute job. The same chicken works in a sandwich, over a salad bowl, or with pasta.
